source_text: Cuius infirmitates ut in praesenti vita diverso remediorum genere mitescunt, ita etiam plene in iustorum tamen corporibus resurrectionis evacuabuntur adventu.
pass_a_gloss: Whose infirmities as in the present life they grow mild by a diverse kind of remedies, so also they will be fully evacuated, yet in the bodies of the just, by the advent of resurrection.
pass_b_english: Just as its infirmities are eased in this present life by various remedies, so they will also be removed completely at the coming resurrection—in the bodies of the righteous, however.

choices.why: Loaded word in Julian's Latin at this locus; English follows LS/Blaise range without copying NPNF.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
